page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.medium is an entry-level general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an AWS Graviton2 processor utilizing 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 1 dedicated vCPU mapping directly to 1 physical core without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 4.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of the general-purpose family. Storage is provided through 59 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance store, offering low-latency direct-attached disk access. Discrete GPU accelerators are not present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate expected baseline behavior for a single-core ARM processor. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1493.49, falling into the median performance band. Because execution is bound to a single thread, multi-core metrics mirror single-core output, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 923.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 658.21. In-memory data throughput reaches 1.18 million Redis SET operations per second, with cached small-block memory reads sustaining 59.37 GB/s and uncached large-block reads registering 19.34 GB/s. Static web serving throughput reaches 1.15 GB/s, while small model (135M) LLM text generation performs at 29.25 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the power profile of the Graviton2 ARM architecture combined with included high-speed NVMe storage. Because the vCPU is dedicated rather than burstable or shared, compute throughput remains consistent without CPU credit exhaustion risks. The primary operational constraint is the single-core ceiling, which limits multi-threaded scalability. The m6gd.medium is technically suited for lightweight web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and localized data processing requiring fast temporary disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.medium is an ARM-based general-purpose server powered by an AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 core operating at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 1 dedicated vCPU, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 59 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. It provides hardware AES encryption acceleration while omitting vector extension units like AVX. Benchmark results demonstrate stable single-threaded throughput, reaching 1493.49 in stress-ng and supporting 1.18 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 1.15 GB/s static web serving throughput. Overall throughput is limited by its single-core configuration, making it unsuitable for highly parallel tasks. The server delivers predictable non-burstable compute and fast ephemeral storage, making it well-suited for lightweight microservices, small caching instances, test environments, and low-traffic web applications.
